summary: A Reddit r/explainlikeimfive archived thread asking how insect legs work and whether they have something like muscle. Commenters explain that many insects have muscles inside the exoskeleton, that some insects and most spiders extend legs using fluid hydraulics while flexing with muscles, and that many insects use spring-loaded exoskeletons to extend legs. The page is surrounded by much unrelated Reddit boilerplate and sidebar content, which is ignored here.
one_line: Reddit thread explaining that insect legs use internal muscles, hydraulic fluid pressure in some insects and spiders, and spring-loaded exoskeletons for movement.
key_facts: The original post was titled "ELI5: How do insect legs work, do they have something like muscle?" and was posted by KlaraNovakRocks in r/explainlikeimfive, tagged Biology.
The post had 381 upvotes and 37 comments when archived, and was about two years old.
Commenter Fredrules2012 said hydraulics are used: insects fill the chambers of their limbs with fluid, which is how bugs hippy hop so strongly and flippy flap so quickly.
KlaraNovakRocks asked what drives the "pump" and valves and whether insects have circulation to move the liquid.
Commenter AdoraBellDearheart said grasshoppers have muscles that work very similarly to mammalian muscles, citing an IB BioNinja page on muscles.
Commenter apple-masher said not all insect legs work the same way and that most insects have muscles located on the inside of the exoskeleton.
According to apple-masher, some insects and most spiders use fluid pressure (hydraulics) to extend their legs and muscles to flex their legs.
According to apple-masher, many insects have spring-loaded legs, using muscles to flex and the springiness of the exoskeleton to extend.
A commenter, AgoraiosBum, jokingly answered the question of why a bug's legs curl up when it dies with "Boneitis."
A commenter, FullCloud, joked about misreading the title as "incest legs."
The sidebar included an unrelated Rice University item saying mechanical engineers repurposed deceased spiders as mechanical grippers.
The sidebar described r/explainlikeimfive as the best forum and archive on the internet for layperson-friendly explanations.
